sections.ayurvedic_treatment_of_childhood_arthrit:
About Childhood Arthritis 
 Childhood Arthritis is known by another name Juvenile Arthritis, is a pediatric rheumatic disease, affecting individuals below the age of 16 years. Chronic and autoimmune disease. It causes pain, swelling, stiffness, and loss of motion. That means the immune system, which normally protects the body from foreign substances, attacks the body instead. The disease is idiopathic, which defines that no exact cause is known. Researchers believe juvenile arthritis may be triggered due to genetics, certain infections, and environmental factors.
sections.symptoms_of_childhood_arthritis:
The most common symptoms of childhood Arthritis is pain, warmth, stiffness, and swelling of joint. Stiffness and swelling are likely to be more severe in the morning. 
 Limping is another symptom that might indicate a particularly severe case of Childhood Arthritis Joint deformity: The joints may grow in an abnormal, asymmetrical way, causing deformities of bone. 
 Skin rash on a child’s arms and legs 
 Fever, comes and go 
 Reduced appetite 
 Weight loss 
 Anemia
sections.other_symptoms_depend_upon_the_types_of_:
Systemic onset arthritis: Affects the whole body. Symptoms include high fever that often increase in the evenings and then may suddenly drop to normal. The spleen and lymph nodes might become enlarged. Many of the body’s joints are affected by pain, swelling, and stiffness. 
 Oligo-articular arthritis: Affects four or less than four joints, often the knee or ankle. Symptoms are pain, stiffness, or swelling in the joints. Severe conditions cause inflammation of eyes. It starts between the ages of two and four years. 
 Polyarticular arthritis : affects five or more joints and occurs between the age of 1 and 12 years. 
 Enthesitis-related arthritis : is a form that often involves attachments of ligaments as well as the spine. 
 Psoriatic arthritis : Strikes some children who have psoriasis (a scaly red rash that can start appearing behind the ears, on the eyelids, elbows, knees, or scalp).
sections.causes_of_childhood_arthritis:
It occurs due to malfunctioning of the Immune System, which mistakenly attacks the body’s own healthy tissues—hence, it is classified as an autoimmune disease. The exact cause of this immune malfunction is not fully understood. However, it is believed to be triggered by a combination of genetic predisposition and environmental factors, such as infections, toxins, stress, or certain medications. In genetically susceptible individuals, these triggers may provoke the immune system to become overactive or misdirected, leading to chronic inflammation and tissue damage. 
 Ayurvedic View 
 Ayurveda describes this disease as occurring due to production of excessive Vata Dosha, defined under the Vyadhi Ama vata. Ama vata is a disease caused as a result of production of Ama (toxic accumulation as a result of reduced digestive activity and obstructed expulsion of foreign substances from the body) that results in joint and systemic symptoms together.
sections.risk_factors: Age: Children from infancy to age of 16, rarely when babies are younger than 6 months old. Children from 2 to 3 years of age are at high risk
sections.gender_girls_are_at_more_risk_than_boys: Genetics: Children with a family history of the disease.
sections.complications_of_childhood_arthritis:
Juvenile arthritis differs from adult arthritis in a way that it causes harm to a child’s still-growing bones and tissues. Though most of the children with the disease will do well in the long run, but inflammation of arthritis can have serious consequences for a child’s growing body including: 

 Overall growth is stunted. 
 Bones may grow too short or too long. 
 Problems in the jaw (that may lead to dental problems, because it can be hard to brush and floss properly). 
 Wearing away or destruction of joints. 
 Inflammation of membranes surrounding the heart or lungs. 
 Loss of vision as a result of chronic eye inflammation (uveitis)
sections.risk_of_osteoarthritis_and_osteoporosis_: Sudden hyperactivity of the immune system called macrophage-activation syndrome (but is extremely rare, potentially life-threatening problem that occurs only in systemic JIA)
